outcome: failure of intrauterine hemorrhage-control devices (unsuccessful arrest of bleeding)
cohort: The study discusses patients experiencing refractory postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony who are treated with intrauterine hemorrhage-control devices.
finding: Failure rates for intrauterine balloon tamponade range from 11-12% and for the Jada device from 7.5% (vaginal) to 16.3% (cesarean), with a significant gap in PPH guidelines regarding the detection and management of device failure.
mod_finding: Failure rates for the Jada device differ by mode of birth, being 7.5% for vaginal deliveries and 16.3% for cesarean deliveries.
